Housing Units per Job: The number of available housing units divided by the total number of jobs in the county. A lower ratio often suggests a housing shortage relative to the workforce.
People per Housing Unit: Total population divided by the total number of housing units. Higher values can indicate overcrowding or a lack of available housing supply.
Jobs per Capita: Total number of jobs divided by the total population. This measures the concentration of employment opportunities relative to the number of residents.
Jobs per Working Age Adult: Total jobs divided by the population aged 18-64. This provides a clearer picture of job availability for the core workforce.
Absolute (Net Flow): The net difference between workers coming into the county and residents leaving the county for work. A positive number means the county is a net employment hub.
Commuter Ratio (In/Out): The ratio of in-commuters to out-commuters. A ratio above 1.0 indicates that more people commute in than commute out.
In-Commuter Job Share (% of Jobs): The percentage of jobs in the county that are filled by people living outside the county.
Resident Retention Share (% of Residents: The percentage of employed residents who both live and work within the county.
Average Age: The weighted average age of the county's residents.
% Residents Under 18: The proportion of the population that is under 18 years old.
% Residents 18-22: The proportion of the population that is in the college-age bracket (18-22).
% Residents 23-34: The proportion of the population that is in the young professional age bracket (23-34).
% Residents 35-49: The proportion of the population in the mid-career age bracket (35-49).
% Residents 50-64: The proportion of the population in the late-career/pre-retirement age bracket (50-64).
% Residents Over 65: The proportion of the population that is 65 years or older.
% Working Age (18-64): The proportion of the population that falls within the traditional working age range of 18-64.
